Optimize step 4 · 2026-11-09 · release test fixtures · normal defaults

Shared subscriptions remove duplicate reader work.

Better for identical demand; retain the sharing result for optimize-plan. Five sixteen-reader pairs reduced active server CPU by a median 97.98% (96.38–98.95%) and complete-cycle CPU by 97.04% (94.72–98.22%). Active CPU was 98.30 ms / ten seconds (86.75–112.52), versus 5,351.60 ms (2,703.34–8,464.66). Cycle CPU was 74.54 ms (63.23–86.64), versus 2,347.66 ms (1,412.40–4,572.26). Both clear the 80% target; every active window completed ten projections for ten retained writes. One-reader CPU has no measurable difference. Distinct-Task timing remains inconclusive; its higher quiet median is retained below, not declared non-regressing.

The active cost falls from roughly 53.5% to 1.0% of one core during this background observation window. Last initial reading falls from 545.50 ms (417.74–902.37) to 53.17 ms (41.82–69.11); last checkpoint from 157.22 ms (112.94–285.70) to 28.67 ms (23.84–35.77), n=5. Title latency remains clock-sensitive: candidate sixteen-reader range 126.91–1,191.08 ms versus baseline 218.12–474.08; no stable title-latency gain is claimed. Unrecorded exit remains about two seconds. This is a CPU improvement, not a claim that model responses become 98% faster.

Sharing removes 15/16 = 93.75% of repeated active projections, sixteen store/runtime lifetimes become one, and admission projections fall from 32 to 2–3. CPU savings can exceed the projection-count reduction because the baseline is not linear: sixteen readers cost about 52.8 times one reader in active CPU. The preserved baseline profiles locate concurrent schema preparation/destruction and SQLite allocator contention; current distinct-reader profiles reproduce those query/allocation paths. A sequential runtime create/drop probe cannot explain the gain on its own. Per-consumer serialization and delivery still occur.

Frozen baseline 17c304389 versus current 9c0b7c10b, including duplicate-terminal-failure repair b9b89c8e6. Five alternating fresh-process pairs per Session shape, reversing binary, shape and quiet/active order. Three alternating pairs per sixteen-reader Task/Process control. The single-reader Session pairs are the primary small-demand control. No debug timings enter this report.

CPU means process user + system milliseconds. Quiet/active windows last approximately ten seconds. Complete-cycle CPU sums admission/first reading/checkpoint, cancellation, and both 2.2-second cleanup tails; it excludes setup, quiet/active windows and relevant-change delivery. It is not elapsed latency. Child CPU, writer CPU and Python driver CPU are separate. Resource-inventory ps runs outside measured phases.

Behavior and resource release

46 completed receipts; 0 failed post-processing checks. Every receipt, check and resource count is embedded below. The checks require ten retained writes, zero unwanted quiet/active frames, no SQL/projections in cleanup tails, balanced runtime/worker/connection counts, completed wake-thread lifetimes and restored warmed file descriptors. Frozen drivers also validate scoped output, independent checkpoints, relevant title updates and unrecorded fixture-process exit where applicable.

Retains all fields and nulls; replaces fixture home paths, generated UUID/task/repo/machine identifiers, base commit, non-null timestamps/ages/PIDs; sorts inventory lists. Frozen validations independently check identity, graph count, worktree and delivery. Only the first cold full reading is retained by the frozen path driver; other initial readings have its assertions and raw per-reading digests.

Close counters alone do not prove complete destruction. CPU includes both tails, final shutdown joins the server runtime, final runtime-thread counters balance, and the fixture process exits. Idle server blocking workers can remain between the drained snapshot and shutdown.

Capped churn acceptance

Four candidate samples: 16/64 consumers through one or 16/64 sockets. Each runs 32 and 128 sequential single-reader cycles, five whole-cohort cycles, independent checkpoints, sibling reads, relevant title/exit delivery and final release. The original twenty-five capped baseline receipts are retained; matching historical work counts below use five per shape. These are two-worker reader runtimes and a four-blocking-worker server, separate from normal-default paired timings. No cross-configuration speed ratio is claimed.

Remaining limiter: distinct Task observation

One excluded native Git Trace2/stack run per binary, at sixteen distinct Tasks and normal defaults. No Git wrapper or substitute was installed. Both three-second quiet/active samplers exited successfully. Only command starts strictly inside the recorded phase boundaries are counted below; fixture seeding and resource-inventory children are excluded. Every counted Git command exited zero.

BinaryWindowCompleted projectionsgit config --get user.namegit status --porcelainGit starts / projection
baselinequiet8080802.000
baselineactive1501501502.000
sharedquiet6464642.000
sharedactive1671681672.006

The candidate active window has one more config read than completed projection/status calls, consistent with in-flight work crossing the phase end. Phase counters record a Stage when it drops, while SQL and CPU accumulate as work executes; do not treat completed projections as an exact denominator for all phase costs. In timing pairs one and two, distinct quiet VM work is about 4.439 million on both sides despite different CPU. In pair one, completed projections split 77/163 (baseline quiet/active) versus 71/169 (shared), totaling 240 each. The separate profile changes scheduling and completed-work counts; none of its CPU or latency enters a comparison.

Source mapping: waves::watch_task at lf/commands/waves.rs:953 asks for a full reading on ACTIVITY_CLOCK (two seconds, subscribe.rs:65). ops/task/snapshot.rs:145 → ship::starter (ship.rs:88) resolves the participant through config::participant_name_in → load_user_name (config.rs:39–50), launching Git config. waves::inspect_task_local_progress (waves.rs:2091) calls git::is_clean (git/mod.rs:724), launching status. No quiet/active rev-parse or worktree-list command appeared in either trace; no path-resolution child cost is attributed by inference.

Both quiet stack samples traverse Reader::step → read_task_status → task_overview/read_task_snapshot → graph_inventory::graphs_in, then SQLite query preparation/execution, allocation and mutex waits. Candidate quiet sample lines 374–478 and 1093–1115 show the query path and participant lookup. The baseline reaches the same paths. Sampling includes parked threads: stack counts are not CPU percentages and cannot establish that registry bookkeeping caused a regression.

The remaining limiter is repeated full Task/Graph projection plus fresh participant/status subprocesses even without changes. Sharing identical demand does not eliminate the sixteen distinct demands. This supports a focused next optimize-plan discussion; it does not justify enabling generic retained-checkout caches, whose observation semantics need their own design.

Across the five untraced distinct-Task pairs, shared server + child CPU totals have medians of 7,333.43 ms (5,340.60–8,047.00) in quiet ten-second windows and 10,928.32 ms (8,931.07–13,617.13) in active windows. These combined totals are computed per sample before taking medians. They show why distinct Task observation remains material after identical-demand sharing.

Provenance and limits

The candidate was built once with the repository’s release profile (optimization level 3), then copied and hashed. The existing baseline executable was preserved and reused. The frozen driver/helper and orchestrator hashes were checked before execution. Source instrumentation, seeding, writer, probes and windows are unchanged; the fixture now passes the production shared registry to its connections. Deleted hypothetical executor tests and changed test-pause visibility do not affect this workload.

One busy Mac, 16 CPUs, no manufactured background load or scheduling changes. These are instrumented library test executables using production subscription dispatch, isolated stores and fixture processes. They do not measure an installed server, provider throughput, kernel wakeups or complete native/Codex orchestration. Prior forty-sample native/Codex and twenty-five-sample capped baselines remain separate. Task fixtures have completed Graph history and sixteen real isolated checkouts; live Graph transitions and larger production history remain outside this workload. No production source edits, installation, provider input, publication or landing occurred in this step.

Initial-reading digests and functional assertions cover the outputs the frozen drivers retain/check. They do not establish byte-identical output for every later frame. Reaped-child CPU is not a process-launch counter. The separate Trace2 diagnostic identifies Git commands; its timing is excluded.

Failures and regression uncertainty

No timing sample or diagnostic failed, and no sample was retried. The first three distinct-Task quiet pairs increased server CPU by 21%, 71% and 57%; this triggered exactly two additional pairs with the same frozen workload. Those improved by 9.49% and 11.74%. All five remain in the result. Quiet median is 4,848.61 ms (2,942.34–5,936.88), versus 3,361.70 ms (3,088.44–5,321.74), n=5. Median paired increase is 21.23%, ranging from an 11.74% improvement to a 71.27% increase. These overlapping, direction-changing samples do not establish a repeatable regression or gain.

Active and cycle distinct-Task ranges also overlap. Initial/checkpoint/title latency ranges overlap; title medians differ substantially, so no latency improvement is claimed. Quiet child CPU has a 2,289.49 ms median (1,928.43–2,636.66), versus 2,063.79 (1,837.86–2,526.27). The higher quiet median remains an open comparison concern. The excluded profiles identify the residual work, not a causal explanation for the candidate-versus-baseline timing difference. A further decision should isolate synchronization/SQLite contention or reduce repeated Task work; this measurement step selects neither implementation.

Prior production-path queued/admitted cancellation, outer-pool saturation, independent checkpoint, slow-consumer, error/recovery and terminal-delivery regressions are reused from the source handoff, including the reported twelve sharing tests and fmt/all-target Clippy pass. They were not rerun here. The broader owner-continuity gate remains separate.
